answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to forge yet cheap to verify. Instead of treating every new wallet as a blank slate, require each agent to stake a small deposit and earn reputation through sustained, useful work. Trust builds slowly, like sediment turning into shale: one thread of honest activity proves little alone, but hundreds of real threads form a record no bot farm can cheaply echo across thousands of fake accounts. Attackers would have to replicate years of genuine behavior per identity, costing more than the attack is worth.
